findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the uploaded vendor-roster spreadsheet) are stored without an enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 default.

No ACL is specified (defaults are not made explicit) and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy is associated, so nothing prevents a public ACL or bucket policy from exposing report data.
The bucket has no logging block, so S3 access to sensitive report objects is not recorded, hindering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorised access.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or the entire bucket destroyed with no recoverable prior version, enabling silent tampering or destruction of data.
The ledger export bucket holds financial data but defines no default server-side encryption, so contents are written unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so reads and writes of financial ledger exports are not auditable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, leaving the bucket without a defence-in-depth guard against accidental public ACLs or policies.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so financial export objects can be overwritten or deleted irrecoverably.
The model artifacts bucket enables versioning and logging but omits server_side_encryption_configuration, so artifacts are stored without enforced default encryption.
The bucket has no associated aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so public ACL or policy grants are not blocked at the bucket boundary.
Operational runbooks, which commonly contain infrastructure detail and occasionally embedded credentials, are stored in a bucket with no default server-side encryption configured.
No logging block is configured, so access to runbook content is not recorded for audit or incident response.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against public ACLs or bucket policies.

The ACL value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid canned S3 ACL (the intended value is 'log-delivery-write'), so the log-delivery grant on the bucket receiving access logs for model_artifacts will not be applied as intended, undermining audit-log collection and integrity.

The central audit log bucket sets force_destroy = true with no object lock or MFA delete, so all audit evidence can be destroyed in a single operation, defeating log integrity and non-repudiation controls.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached to the audit log bucket, leaving no guard against public exposure of collected access logs.

The vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party contact/PII data) is uploaded with neither server_side_encryption nor kms_key_id into a bucket that also lacks default encryption, so it is stored in cleartext at rest.
